appraisal_events.evidence: Albertine relates, laughing, that Gilberte once drove her home and kissed her and «me demanda tout d'un coup si j'aimais les femmes», to which she answered yes «pour la mystifier», «mais nous ne fîmes rien du tout»; each claim is met by a parenthesis undoing it — «si elle ne faisait que croire se rappeler que Gilberte l'avait ramenée, comment pouvait-elle dire avec tant de précision que Gilberte lui avait posé cette question bizarre ?», «C'était étrange, si elles avaient échangé ces confidences, qu'elles n'eussent rien fait», «On aurait dit qu'Albertine craignait que Gilberte m'eût raconté cela» — while the listener notes «J'eus beaucoup de peine à ne poser aucune question, mais, me dominant pour avoir l'air de n'attacher à tout cela aucune importance».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narration dismantles her confidence as it is being made, so the anecdote she offers as amusing lowers her credibility, while the man who hears it must silently swallow every question he wants to ask.

appraisal_events.evidence: She interrupts the lecture on Hardy, Stendhal, Vermeer and Dostoïevski to ask what he had meant by «le côté Dostoïevski de Mme de Sévigné», «Je vous avoue que je n'ai pas compris», and later «est-ce qu'il a jamais assassiné quelqu'un, Dostoïevski ?»; he concedes twice — «ce que j'avais dit là était assez bête», «c'est très tiré par les cheveux» — while rewarding her: «Venez, petite fille, que je vous embrasse pour vous remercier de vous rappeler si bien ce que je dis, vous retournerez au pianola après.»
appraisal_events.explanation: Her questions extract two admissions from the lecturer, but the praise she wins is for remembering his own words and comes with a kiss and a dismissal back to the pianola, so her gain is granted on his terms.

status_effects.explanation: The narration presents her account as internally inconsistent and defensively timed, so she comes off as someone caught arranging her story.
He is the one who suffers and conceals it, forced to feign indifference and to hold back the questions the story provokes.
Her plain questions make the lecturer retract his own formula as silly and far-fetched, and win explicit praise for the accuracy of her memory.

ambiguities: The passage never settles whether Albertine is lying: the contradictions are registered only as the listener's parenthetical questions, and his jealousy is itself the reason he is counting them, so the diminishment rests on suspicion the text leaves unconfirmed.
